hermes_plugin_state: The opencode SKILL.md (v1.2.0) provides: install via `npm i -g opencode-ai@latest` or WinGet; auth via `opencode auth login` or provider env vars; verify with `opencode auth list`; one-shot tasks via `opencode run 'prompt'`; model forcing via `--model provider/model`; `--format json` for machine-readable output; `--file` to attach files; session management (`--continue`, `--session`, `--agent`); PR review workflow; parallel work with separate workdirs. Missing for fleet dispatch: direct Space Bunny/Zen free lane dispatch patterns, fleet-scale orchestration, non-interactive Zen API patterns, programmatic auth for free lane. The skill documents bounded coding tasks but not fleet bot dispatch workflows.
install_login: On Windows: install via WinGet (SST.opencode_Microsoft.Winget.Source_8wekyb3d8bbwe) providing v1.18.30, or `npm i -g opencode-ai@latest`. Auth: `opencode auth login` (browser OAuth flow) or set provider env vars (e.g., OPENROUTER_API_KEY). Verify: `opencode auth list` should show at least one provider. Three stored credentials in auth.json: OpenCode Zen api, OpenRouter api, alibaba-cloud api. To switch accounts: `opencode providers logout [provider]` then `opencode providers login [url]`, or set different provider env vars.
multiple_accounts: Yes, multiple accounts can coexist. auth.json stores 3 credentials (OpenCode Zen api, OpenRouter api, alibaba-cloud api). Switch between accounts via `opencode providers logout [provider]` followed by `opencode providers login [url]`, or by setting different provider environment variables for different OpenCode sessions. All credentials persist in ~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json.
noninteractive_usage: `opencode run 'Add retry logic to API calls'` — one-shot execution, no pty needed. `--model provider/model` forces specific model (e.g., `--model space-bunny-free`). `--format json` produces machine-readable JSON events/output. Working directory set via `cd` before running or the shell's cwd. Stdout captured in command output; exit code returned by the tool (0 = success, non-zero = error). Example: `cd /path/to/project && opencode run --model space-bunny-free --format json "implement OAuth refresh"`. For timeout: wrap in script timeout mechanism; check %ERRORLEVEL% after completion.
spacebunny_lane: Space Bunny Free model (`space-bunny-free`) available through OpenCode Zen gateway. Model ID: space-bunny-free. Endpoint: https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/chat/completions. AI SDK package: @ai-sdk/openai-compatible. Free stealth model with zero-retention policy (no data used for model training). Selected via CLI flag: `--model space-bunny-free`. Part of OpenCode Zen — optional gateway; you don't need to use it to use OpenCode. Free for a limited time. Documented model selection: `--model space-bunny-free` or configure in provider settings as `space-bunny-free`/`@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`.
summary: OpenCode CLI v1.18.30 is installed on Windows via WinGet. Auth configured with 3 stored credentials (OpenCode Zen, OpenRouter, alibaba-cloud). `opencode run 'prompt'` enables one-shot non-interactive execution. Model selection uses `--model provider/model` flag. Hermes agent skill (opencode SKILL.md v1.2.0) integrates OpenCode as a delegate coding worker providing install, auth, and one-shot task commands. However, the OpenCode Zen free lane (Space Bunny Free) requires browser-based OAuth authentication that the programmatic API cannot replicate — CLI has bundled session/credential access, raw API returns HTTP 403. Fleet dispatch must go through the CLI, not the API. Recommended dispatch pattern: `opencode run --model space-bunny-free --format json "PROMPT"` with working directory set and exit code checked.
why_api_fails_cli_works: The OpenCode Zen free lane (including Space Bunny Free) requires browser-based OAuth authentication with session cookies, CSRF tokens, and device fingerprinting that the programmatic API cannot replicate. Evidence: (1) API probes to the Space Bunny / OpenCode Zen free lane return HTTP 403 from server-side auth checks; (2) Running `opencode` CLI directly (seated at the machine) works because it has bundled authentication — stored API keys in auth.json plus browser session persistence; (3) The programmatic API path can provide API keys but lacks the full browser-derived session credentials (OAuth flow, fingerprints, same-site cookies) that OpenCode Zen requires; (4) The local opencode.db "no such column: project_id" error may also impede programmatic model listing/selection, though the CLI may bypass this through different code paths. The CLI works because it bundles the authenticated session; the API requires re-establishing the full browser-derived auth context that cannot be programmatically reproduced.
